text: People sin when they try to get rich, and they convince themselves they are not being dishonest.
But sin is stuck tightly between buying and selling, just like a wooden peg hammered between two stones in a wall.
And if you disobey the Lord, your home[59] will soon be destroyed.
Impurities can easily be seen after flour is sifted and after someone speaks.
The quality of a clay dish is seen in the heat of the pottery furnace, just as our true character is seen in what we say.
Fruit shows how much care a tree has received, and our words show the care we have given to our minds.
So don't start praising people, until you hear what they say.
Make fairness your goal; you will reach it and receive great honor.
Just as birds of the same kind come together in a flock, people will be honest with you, if you are honest with them.
But sin is watching like a lion and is ready to gobble you up if you do evil.
Good people always speak wisely, but you never can tell what a fool will say next.
Don't waste your time listening to stupid people; spend it with those who know how to think.
It is disgusting to listen to fools laughing about their sins. *
Their cursing and arguing makes your hair stand on end and your ears ache.
But fools are too proud to stop sinning, until someone gets hurt.
Your friends won't trust you or like you anymore if you can't keep a secret.
If you don't tell their secrets, your friends will know that you really like them. But if you tell their secrets, they won't want you around,
and your friendship is as dead as a soldier killed by the enemy.
It is gone for good, like a captive bird that has been set free
or a deer that has escaped from a trap. So don't bother trying to get back that friendship.
Wounds can be bandaged and insults forgiven, but nothing can heal the harm of telling someone's secret.
Stay away from those who wink and plan to deceive others.
They tell you how great you are and how well you speak, but later, they twist your words to make you look bad.
I hate people like them more than anything else, and even the Lord hates them.
Striking a friend is the same as throwing a stone straight up in the air— you will be the one who gets hurt.
And you will get caught in traps that you set to cheat others.
No one seems to realize that evil always returns to the one who does it.
Proud people insult others, but revenge will follow them like a lion stalking a victim.
When God's people are in trouble, those who make fun of them will die in terrible pain, like an animal in a trap.
Taking revenge in anger is disgusting—yet sinners just won't give it up.
